products.note: Enterprise content AI; metadata; governance; compliance; retention policies

reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is a public company founded in 2005 and headquartered in Redwood City, California, traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker BOX. It files with the SEC as BOX INC under CIK 0001372612, and its most recent reported revenue, for the period ending 2026-01-31 on Form 10-K, was $1,177,253,000. On its own site the company describes an Intelligent Content Management platform for storing, sharing, editing, and co-creating unstructured content such as sales presentations, product specs, employee handbooks, lease agreements, and finance documents, with enterprise security and compliance features the site says address requirements including GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA.

Its tracked product is Box AI, listed under Notes, Knowledge and Meetings, which the site describes as enterprise content AI with metadata, governance, compliance, and retention policies. According to the site, Box AI connects to models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google for summaries, analysis, and recommendations, and the platform includes a drag-and-drop workflow builder, agents, AI-driven threat detection and malware detection, automated classification, access controls, e-signature workflows, and Box AI Studio for customizing agents. The site also states that Box was named a Leader with the highest scores possible in 13 criteria including innovation, vision, security, and AI/ML.

The record also lists a California law exposure count of 281. Nine MCP servers are tracked in connection with Box, including ai.clize/inbox, ai.ironshard/agent-storage-sandbox, ai.powerline/inbox-preview, ai.slidingbox/hydrate-dehydrate, ai.smithery/cindyloo-dropbox-mcp-server, ai.smithery/smithery-toolbox, ai.surfingdog/inbox, ai.thoughtbox.api/thoughts, and bot.mailbox/mailbox. No lawsuits are recorded.
